subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: Meta-Analysis: Combining Studies for Stronger Answers
description: A short lesson to help you apply Meta-Analysis: Combining Studies for Stronger Answers.

hook.text: One study says coffee prevents cancer. Another says it causes cancer.

buildup.text: Meta-analysis: statistically combining results from multiple studies to find an overall effect size.

discovery.text: By pooling data, meta-analyses have more statistical power — they can detect small effects that individual studies miss.

twist.text: Garbage in, garbage out. A meta-analysis of poorly designed studies produces a precise but wrong answer.

climax.text: The Cochrane Collaboration produces the world's most trusted meta-analyses — the basis for evidence-based medicine.

punchline.text: One study is a hint. A meta-analysis is the closest thing to an answer.

quiz.question: What is a meta-analysis?
options: An analysis of the analysis method
A statistical combination of results from multiple studies
A review of a single study

details.summary: Meta-analysis statistically combines results from multiple studies to produce a more precise estimate of an effect. By pooling data, it overcomes the limitations of small individual studies and reveals patterns invisible in single experiments.
details.whyItMatters: Individual studies are limited by sample size and local conditions. Meta-analysis provides the most reliable summary of what the evidence collectively shows.
takeaways: Meta-analysis pools results from many studies for greater precision
It can detect small effects that individual studies miss
Quality depends entirely on the quality of included studies

faq.question: What is the difference between a meta-analysis and a systematic review?
faq.answer: A systematic review comprehensively identifies and evaluates all relevant studies on a question. A meta-analysis goes further by statistically combining the results. Systematic reviews can exist without the quantitative pooling step.

faq.question: What is the biggest risk in relying on a meta-analysis?
faq.answer: Garbage in, garbage out. If the included studies are poorly designed, biased, or heterogeneous, combining them statistically produces a precise but inaccurate answer. The quality of the underlying studies is everything.
